Criteria.Skill: Correct center O=(0,1) inferred from at least two full-polygon corresponding point pairs and verified by all three radii and CCW90
True separate-card information gap with questions for O, angle, direction; partner interchange documented and reconstructed full labelled image
Correct translation (+2,0) then x=0 reflection coordinates and reversed order, fully labelled triangles
Original Edulytiks Cool-down exact and reproducible ordered composition, side/angle preservation and order-sensitive reasoning

privateAnswerKey.doubleAxisReflection: Reflect across x-axis then y-axis maps (x,y)→(-x,-y); 180-degree rotation about origin.

correct: Center O=(0,1), all three vertices rotate 90° CCW to P′(0,3),Q′(-2,3),R′(-1,2)
Problem/data partner roles separated with explicit O(0,1), 90° CCW requested only when needed
Cool-down reverse-order image (1,1),(-1,1),(1,2) differs from forward
equivalent: Rotation center found by intersecting perpendicular bisectors of corresponding chords or by coordinate geometry
Complete spoken descriptions and labelled diagrams equivalent to fully written reasoning
Two axis reflections through O equivalent to 180° turn about O; 180° clockwise and CCW are equivalent
wrong: Center (0,0) wrongly used for P(2,1) to P′(0,3)
Claiming a single point pair identifies the unique polygon rotation without full vertex checks
Making data holder solve and expose the entire data card before question exchange
Reflect first then translate falsely described as identical to translate then reflect
Incorrect reverse-order final coordinates or omitted angle direction
malformed: Missing at least one of P′ Q′ R′ labels
No center/angle/direction requested from data holder
No partner card exchange record or student reconstruction
Only numeric P′ without polygon-wide justification
boundary: Same center O=(0,1) can be shown using equivalent geometric bisectors or coordinate calculations
Equal radius alone for ONE pair does not prove entire 90° rotation
Data card and problem card must not be displayed together in the information-gap round
Order of operations changes outcome for horizontal translation and reflection across x=0
Point lying on axis x=0 remains fixed under that reflection, yet translation can move it
Correct complete alternate spoken geometric explanation may substitute for writing under educator judgment
